questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Germany and it was important that the city was nice to live in as a student.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not very easy, I think the information was spread out on to many different platforms

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I attended the introduction week, which was helpful, but not really any "assistance" I guess.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The university just had a big digitalisation of their system, which made it difficult for the "tutors" to inform us well on how to do the different things.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not the easiest.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's okay, but I had preferred to get something through Studentenwerk

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember it well, but I didn't find it easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: People at Uni was helpful, but I often had to write to several people to figure out what to do.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately there were about 2-3 classes that I wanted to have that I didn't get because they were full, which was quite frustrating.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To register before going to the classes. We were told(and informed online by former erasmus students) that you could just go to a class and then be signed up - this was not the case for me in all classes, because some lectures/teachers already had a full list of people who wanted to attend the class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Too much work for too few ECTS.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A really high level in general - I was almost only in classes that were taught in english with a lot of international students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We had more group work, and sometimes a bit too much for me. But it made sense since it was seminars, where I'm used to more of a mix between lectures and group work. I think it was a bit annoying that there were almost no lectures in my field, so I had to choose seminars.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Debates across World Regions: Socio-Ecological Transformations in Energy and Food 
Food movements
Humanitarianism, Charity and Volunteering
Don't skip class: Advances in Research on Social Class and Adolescent Development
Diversität, Differenzierung und Inklusion

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked the courses I had on Bildungswissenschaft, because I found them easier to follow(since it's my field). But I actually found all my courses interesting, the workload was just a bit overwhelming.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I moved from my student dorm to another private flat after 3 months, which costed me almost 2 months extra rent, since I couldn't quit the first contract.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The canteen was cheap
Experiences was expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I payed for some kayaking and a fitness card at the Uni hochschulesport, which I didn't think was really worth the money.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Language exchange, hochschulesport(that you have to pay for), different sport on tv in the canteen, events and a couple of festivals

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The fesitvals at Mensa were great 
Visiting the city's pools in the summer.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Karlstor Bahnhof has some nice events, festivals and parties.
Trips to the different small cities nearby, but also München, Stuttgart and so on.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Good idea to meet with your buddy and just show up to the different uni events

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That you can not always pay with credit card

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: In general I found people friendly and down to earth.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The bureaucracy is annoying, but things will work out in the end(most of the time)
Show up to the ESN events in the beginning to make friends - It didn't seemed like people were socializing in class.
Enjoy the surrounding landscapes with some hikes or bike rides!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of more than what I have already written

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I made great friends, I got better in both german and english and I think Heidelberg is a nice city to live in for a semester!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To figure out which courses I could take, the workload and the bureaucracy!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
